extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of natural philosophy, evolution, comparative linguistics, and the arts
extracted.subtask_description: Identify and describe the criteria by which systems (languages, sciences, arts, organisms, planets, societies) exhibit progressive integration (coherence, unity) and simultaneous differentiation (complexity, multiformity). Applicable to analytic or expository work that assesses evolutionary change across domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration in language via agglutination and coalescence
rubrics_metrics.description: Compound words in 'uncivilized' languages are often many-syllabled; progressively, languages reduce polysyllables to di- and monosyllables by coalescence (agglutination → amalgamation → anaptotic languages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Kicaree and Pawnee long words for common objects; Anglo-Saxon steorra → English star, mona → moon, nama → name. Frequency of repetition drives contraction (e.g. smithas → smiths; cuman → come). Compound vowels fuse (bread pronounced bred). Where repetition is greatest, coalescence is carried furthest (examples: la ford → lord; 'God be with you' → 'Good-bye').

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammatical development enabling coherence (from aptotic to inflected forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Languages evolve from 'aptotic' (separate words expressing relations) through agglutinate (inflectional adjuncts traceable to separate words) to amalgamate languages (inflections no longer traceable), enabling closer union of proposition elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast Chinese (aptotic) where relations are expressed by separate words with languages where adjuncts become annexes; the emergence of inflections/connective words allows sentences whose parts are mutually dependent and less changeable without destroying meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence-level aggregation and subordinate complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: As grammatical forms develop, sentences show increased aggregation: more subordinate propositions, complements, and qualifying clauses linking into complex wholes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare Hebrew scriptures (simpler, single-subject sentences) with modern writings (multiple subordinate clauses and complex aggregation). Increased ability to form complex sentences is a sign of linguistic integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration in science via classification and generalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific progress is marked by uniting confused popular aggregations into compact, nested groups (classes, orders, genera) and by generalizing relations across phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: zoological classification (Vertebrata, Annulosa, Mollusca), colligation of concrete relations into lowest-order generalizations and then into higher ones; Humboldt's linking of audible torrent murmurs, visibility of remote objects, and coming rain; integration of Electricity, Magnetism, and Light into unified theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical and industrial integration (machines and factory systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advancement from simple tools to complex machines composed of multiple integrated simple agents; factories exemplify large-scale integration of many machines driven by a common motive power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: lever → wheel-and-axle → modern spinning/weaving apparatus combining many primitives; locomotive combining fire-box, boiler, and machinery; factories where many machines are connected by shafts to a single steam-engine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of composition in visual arts as a test of merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Progress in the arts shows increased subordination of parts to an organic whole; merit is tested by successful unity of effect drawn from variety of components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast ancient Egyptian/Assyrian mural groups that can be separated with little loss of meaning with modern historical paintings where attitudes, expressions, lights, and colours are coordinated. Medieval tapestries display miscellanea; modern works show a distinct centre and coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration in music—melody, harmony, and orchestral unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Musical integration progresses from simple repeated cadences to long melodies with multiple voice parts, harmonies, accompaniment, and orchestral ensembles where parts subordinate to a total effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: chant cadences → long combined musical phrases; addition of bass, tenor, alto; chorus and orchestral effects integrated into musical drama; the melody's inability to be broken without loss indicates integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary integration—cohesion of plot and interdependent characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Literary evolution moves from disconnected sequences of adventures to works where events follow from characters under given conditions and characters' minds influence one another—parts are interdependent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primitive tales (Eastern story-tellers) present successive unconnected occurrences; good modern imaginative works present events as necessary products of character and conditions; changing order or kind of events injures overall effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary aspect of evolution: increase in coherence (integration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evolution is, primarily, change from a less coherent form to a more coherent form, consequent on dissipation of motion and integration of matter, observable across cosmic, organic, and social orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This universality is evidenced in solar system evolution, organism development, and social products like science; unification proceeds in several ways simultaneously (aggregation of mass, consolidation of parts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual dependence as indicator of integration
rubrics_metrics.description: A higher degree of development is marked by parts forming a cooperative assemblage whose mutual dependence makes considerable change destructive of the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: organisms that die if a part is lost vs. simple organisms that can be cut into pieces and survive; societies and sciences where divisions are mutually dependent and require one another's aid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compound evolution: differentiation accompanying integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Where primary integration is accompanied by secondary redistributions, complexity and heterogeneity arise — components become differentiated while the whole integrates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition: primary redistribution (diffuse → concentrated) accompanied by secondary redistributions (homogeneous → heterogeneous). The components of a mass become more multiform as they coalesce. This is framed as the universal expression of structural modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Astronomical differentiation as evidence of compound evolution
rubrics_metrics.description: The sidereal system shows growing variety of structure—nebulas (diffused, spiral, annular), star groups (sparse to globular), contrasts in star size, colour, spectra—indicating differentiation concurrent with aggregation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solar System example: gaseous spheroid cooled and left annular portions, leading to sun, planets, satellites differing in bulk, weight, temperature, orbits, axes, and physical constitutions; these secondary redistributions increased heterogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geological differentiation: Earth's crust and climate heterogeneity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Earth's cooling and solidifying produced surface differentiation (strata, igneous rocks, faults, mountain systems) and climate differentiation (polar to tropical regimes), making localities distinct in contour, geologic structure, and chemistry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processes: cooling and deposition of solidifiable elements, precipitation of water, condensation beginning at poles, multiplication of strata, tilting of sedimentary layers, igneous intrusion, elevation/subsidence—resulting in increasingly varied local meteorologic and geologic conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological differentiation—chemical composition and tissue specialization
rubrics_metrics.description: Development of plants and animals shows initial homogeneous germ substances becoming chemically segregated and structurally differentiated into varied compounds, tissues, and organs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: vegetal embryo materials giving rise to chlorophyll, cellulose, wax, starch → sugar/gum/isomers; in animals protein, fats, salts localize to form blood, nerve tissue, cartilage, bone; cells differentiate into tissues (chlorophyll-cells, spongy leaf parenchyma), vessels form via lined cells, and tissues re-differentiate into organs.
